concepts.title: Infrastructure: The Engine of Development
concepts.definition: Infrastructure is the vast network of tangible structures and systems a country runs on, roads, ports, power plants, telephone lines and telecom towers; it is the engine that pulls development forward.
concepts.key_idea: Infrastructure is the economy's skeleton: goods, power and messages move only as well as the network allows.

concepts.title: Roads, Railways and Metro Systems
concepts.definition: Transport infrastructure carries people and goods: India's expanding network of national highways, over 68,000 km of railway tracks among the world's longest, and metro trains now running in 23 Indian cities.
concepts.key_idea: Distance shrinks when roads, rails and metros grow: markets widen and journeys shorten.

concepts.title: Energy and Digital Infrastructure
concepts.definition: Power plants and grids light homes and run factories, while telephone lines, towers and optical fibre carry voices and data; energy and digital networks together multiply what every other sector can do.
concepts.key_idea: Electricity and connectivity are enablers: a clinic, a school and a factory all stand still without them.

concepts.title: Infrastructure and the Quality of Life
concepts.definition: APJ Abdul Kalam's dream of a developed India wants the same roads, power, water and communication in village and city; the chapter's graphs of railways, ports and metro length show infrastructure raising living standards.
concepts.key_idea: Development is measured in access: when village and city share the same infrastructure, opportunity spreads.
